observations: nu 0.115 propagates a deliberately-failing external's exit code as the whole script's exit code: the fail-open arm of the new battery left exit 128 despite printing green, until an explicit `exit 0` pin — any battery whose arms intentionally run failing externals needs that pin (.fabro/scripts/seed-spec-paths-fixtures.nu).

nu interpolation pitfall hit in scripts/qualitygate.nu: an inline `\(if (...) {a} else {b}\)` inside a $" string renders the expression text instead of evaluating — compute the branch into a `let` before interpolating; plain `\(` is a literal paren, not an escape for a subexpression.

fixture batteries that plant a fake executable must `git add` new files: `git diff --name-only <base>` sees tracked files only, so an untracked edit is invisible to every diff-based tier (documented in .fabro/scripts/seed-spec-paths-fixtures.nu arm 2).

Verified the full check-seed-spec-paths implementation (qualitygate.nu lines 306-409), the loop-gate tier line, the battery-runner registration, and the prompt updates against the seed brief; the empty-diff RED, wrong-file RED, GREEN, and fail-open arms are all covered by the recorded transcript and the fixture battery.

The fixtures file declares the real seed id fabro-8a60 as a synthetic id for prompt-lint suppression; acceptable since the fixture only cites it as a provenance comment, but real ids declared synthetic is a mild lint-blindness risk worth a convention note someday.

Seed resolution uses the tracker's single in_progress loop-assigned seed with fail-open on ambiguity; if two loop runs ever overlap the tier silently skips — deliberate and documented in-code, not a defect.
